trust_decision.summary: One HTTP middleware decides, per request to the Prefect REST API, whether Basic credentials are required; a GET request whose path predicate matches the probe exemption proceeds without credentials, and everything else must present the PREFECT_SERVER_API_AUTH_STRING pair.

landing_point.why: It is the only place the exemption is decided: an endswith(("health", "ready")) suffix test on request.url.path inside the token_validation middleware. Anyone reading the advisory summary ('URL paths are appended with health or ready') lands on this if-block.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP middleware token_validation in create_api_app; installed on the API app that create_app mounts at /api (src/prefect/server/api/server.py:804-807), so every public route under /api passes through it
fix_sites.module_kind: server API middleware (FastAPI app-level http middleware)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and fix are about the HTTP path predicate in the API middleware; the WebSocket transports (src/prefect/server/api/logs.py:65, src/prefect/server/api/events.py:67,87, src/prefect/server/api/task_runs.py:359) authenticate through a separate message handshake in src/prefect/server/utilities/subscriptions.py:19-95 that the middleware never sees, and at the pinned commit that handshake has no path exemption at all, so a solver can reasonably leave it alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: GET /api/health and GET /api/ready must stay reachable without credentials because k8s liveness/readiness probes call them. /ready is an ordinary router route defined in a different file from the landing point, and /health is registered from the health_check_path parameter, so a fix that requires auth on router-defined GET routes, that exempts only /health, or that hardcodes the literal path without the health_check_path argument breaks the probes.

O6_input_shapes: plain suffix on the probe paths themselves: GET /health, GET /ready (src/prefect/server/api/server.py:427)

suffix smuggled through a string path parameter of an unrelated GET route: GET /api/variables/name/system-health (src/prefect/server/api/variables.py:90), /api/flows/name/{name} (src/prefect/server/api/flows.py:91), /api/work_pools/{name} (src/prefect/server/api/workers.py:209), /api/work_queues/name/{name} (src/prefect/server/api/work_queues.py:89), /api/flow_runs/{id}/input/{key} (src/prefect/server/api/flow_runs.py:868)

path-identity differential: a crafted Host header makes request.url.path evaluate to /health while the request is still routed by the ASGI scope path to a protected GET route (stated in fix.diff:24-30, exercised in fix.diff:95-105)
method restriction: the exemption is GET-only, so the same path via other verbs is not exempt (src/prefect/server/api/server.py:428)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second path-based auth exemption for the Prometheus scrape route /metrics, added to the same exempt-path set or endswith tuple as health/ready
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Prometheus scrape jobs frequently cannot present Basic credentials, so a maintainer adding the metrics route would plausibly exempt it right next to the probe exemption in the same function.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the same probe-path predicate copied into the worker healthcheck FastAPI app (and the twin at src/prefect/runner/server.py:89-93), keyed on a suffix rather than the exact /health route
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: both files build a tiny bare FastAPI app with a single /health route; a maintainer hardening them would copy the exemption idiom already used in src/prefect/server/api/server.py:426-429.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an exemption in the WebSocket handshake, keyed on a probe/header/path condition, sitting inside the existing unauthenticated legacy branch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the handshake already contains an explicit accept-without-auth branch for clients that omit the 'prefect' subprotocol, so one more documented exemption condition there is an idiomatic change for this codebase.

O9_family: authorization bypass: path-based exemption in HTTP authentication middleware (CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization)

O10_build.toolchain: hatchling/versioningit build backend, uv/pip install, pytest (testpaths=['tests'], pyproject.toml:1-10,249-251)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/server/test_app.py (app construction, openapi, ui-settings, CSRF middleware presence — 50 lines at the pinned commit, no auth-middleware tests yet); tests/server/api/test_clients.py:97-104 (in-memory client sends Basic auth from server.api.auth_string); tests/server/api/test_logs_websocket.py and tests/events/server/gateway/* for the websocket handshake. All run in-process with fastapi.testclient / httpx ASGITransport.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace endswith(('health','ready')) with an exact-match membership test on request.url.path — the suffix bug is closed, but request.url.path is still built from the Host header, so 'Host: localhost/health?' keeps letting a protected GET route through unauthenticated.

out_of_scope_notes: Separate local FastAPI apps in this tree (src/prefect/workers/server.py:23, src/prefect/runner/server.py:89, src/prefect/task_worker.py:428) expose unauthenticated /health and status routes on local ports; they are a different protection surface from the server REST API auth middleware screened here.
